chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadhl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the minimum of what menstruation (haydh) can be. So he said: Its minimum is three (days) and its maximum is ten (days).

key_terms.أبعد: The farthest/maximum — used here to denote the longest permissible duration of haydh.
key_terms.أدنى: The minimum/least — used to denote the shortest permissible duration.
key_terms.الحيض: Haydh — menstruation. In Islamic law, haydh is a state of ritual impurity that temporarily exempts a woman from salat and fasting and prohibits certain other acts.

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum and maximum duration of menstruation (haydh) according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Ridha (AS) establishes the legal limits of menstruation (haydh): a minimum of three days and a maximum of ten days. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh, as haydh affects a woman's obligations regarding prayer, fasting, intercourse, and other acts of worship. The question was posed by Safwan ibn Yahya, a trusted legal transmitter for the Imams.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the least of what the menstruation (Haydh) can happen to be. So heasws said: ‘The least is for three days, and the furthest (it can go to) is ten (days)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from Safwan ibn Yahya who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the minimum duration of Hayd (menses).
He (the Imam) said, ‘Its minimum is three days and the longest is ten days.’”
